name: Harribance: equal bilateral LTP, 20-s rotation, alternating with no field
origin: Persinger & Koren lab (Laurentian University), later Koren Helmet trials with the psychic Sean Harribance, reported in Persinger 2010
summary: A later Harribance series from Persinger's lab: the same LTP pattern at equal strength on both sides over the parietotemporal regions, stepping around the four coil pairs once every 20 s instead of every 2 s, here alternated with no-field blocks. Persinger reported that it cut Harribance's alpha rhythm to 25-30% of baseline and the rated accuracy of his readings by about 20% (one subject).
notes: Persinger 2010 (p. 454) reports that in several later trials the same LTP pattern, applied at equal strength over both parietotemporal regions with one complete rotation taking 20 s instead of 2 s, lowered his alpha rhythm to 25-30% of baseline and his accuracy, as rated by others, by about 20%. The number and length of trials are not given, so this program alternates three 5-min no-field and LTP blocks (an assumption) so field and no-field periods can be compared. Persinger 2010 describes the Koren Helmet as four pairs of solenoids "arranged in an elliptical pattern at the level of temporoparietal region", fed by a commutator that sends the pattern to each of the four pairs in turn (0.5 s each in the first series); Persinger & Murphy 2016 add that one solenoid on the left and one on the right are on at any moment. The fields were "weak (1 uT)". Here each side carries four coils on a small ellipse over the temporoparietal region (T7, C5, CP5, TP7 and T8, C6, CP6, TP8), stepped in mirror image; the exact positions and stepping order are not published. Equal strength on both sides, 5 s per pair. LTP is described as "a single pulse followed about 170 msec later by 4 pulses in rapid succession with a functional frequency of between 100 and 200 Hz"; it is built as 1-ms positive pulses at 0, 170, 175, 180 and 185 ms, repeating every 200 ms. The repetition rate is not given; 5 per second follows the lab's "1 s pulse of 5 trains" LTP field (Delparte & Persinger 2007). The 200-Hz spacing (the top of the stated range, which keeps the next primer 15 ms clear of the burst), the polarity, the 1-ms points and the repetition rate are assumptions; the project's primed generator instead uses the 150-ms primer interval of a later Shiva LTP file (Corradini 2014) with 100-Hz pulses. The "Harribance configuration" of Persinger & Saroka 2012 is his own digitised EEG and is not part of this program. One subject, unblinded, a reported reduction rather than a gain; it is most useful as a comparison condition for persinger-harribance-koren-2s. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on headache, nausea or distress.
setting: Seated, eyes closed or blindfolded, in a quiet, dark room. In each block, describe a hidden photograph that someone else picked at random, and have a third person rate the descriptions against the photographs without knowing which blocks had the field (use the app's Blind option).
schedule: Several trials with one subject in the original; their number and spacing are not given.
source: Persinger 2010, The Harribance effect as pervasive out-of-body experiences, NeuroQuantology 8(4):444-465, pp. 448-449 and 454 http://web.archive.org/web/20150426091303id_/http://www.neuroquantology.com/index.php/journal/article/download/301/346 ; Persinger & Murphy 2016, Neuroscience & Medicine 7:27-44 (Koren Helmet: four left-right solenoid pairs, 0.5 s each, 2-s cycle) https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/god-helmet/god_helmet_debate_publication.htm ; Persinger & Saroka 2012, Protracted parahippocampal activity associated with Sean Harribance, Int J Yoga 5:140-145 https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3410194/ ; Delparte & Persinger 2007, Int J Neurosci 117:295-299 (LTP field as "1 s pulse of 5 trains") https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17365115/ ; Corradini 2014, MA thesis, Laurentian University (primed-burst LTP file) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/1455e1f3-2f1d-47b5-93cd-23713d69e651 ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1-6 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
